    1|       |//! Exact active-set audits for solver candidates.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Active-set methods are useful proposal strategies, but the active mask is
    4|       |//! not proof. This module audits the caller's active/inactive constraint flags
    5|       |//! by replaying every residual exactly and certifying the signed residual
    6|       |//! status before accepting the mask. Equality and soft rows are expected to be
    7|       |//! active. Inequalities are expected to be active exactly when binding and
    8|       |//! inactive exactly when strictly satisfied. Violations are reported regardless
    9|       |//! of the mask. This keeps active-set decisions inside the exact decision
   10|       |//! boundary; see the exact-geometric-computation model. The active-set terminology follows
   11|       |//! the standard nonlinear-programming/KKT convention; see standard nonlinear-optimization methods.
   12|       |

  448|       |/// floating tolerances, drive every branch.

 1379|       |        #[test]
 1380|       |        fn generated_less_equal_active_masks_follow_exact_sign(
 1381|       |            residual in -64_i16..=64,
 1382|       |            active in proptest::bool::ANY,
 1383|       |        ) {
 1384|       |            let residual = i64::from(residual);
 1385|       |            let mut problem = Problem::default();
 1386|       |            problem.add_variable("x", real(0));
 1387|       |            let mut constraint = Constraint::equality("generated inequality", Expr::int(residual));
 1388|       |            constraint.kind = ConstraintKind::LessOrEqual;
 1389|       |            constraint.active = active;
 1390|       |            problem.add_constraint(constraint);
 1391|       |
 1392|       |            let report = audit_active_set(
 1393|       |                &problem.analyze(),
 1394|       |                &crate::eval::context_from_problem(&problem),
 1395|       |                CandidateCertificationConfig::default(),
 1396|       |            );
 1397|       |
 1398|       |            let status = &report.rows[0].status;
 1399|       |            match (active, residual.cmp(&0)) {
 1400|       |                (_, std::cmp::Ordering::Greater) => {
 1401|       |                    assert!(matches!(status, ActiveSetRowStatus::CertifiedViolation { .. }));
 1402|       |                }
 1403|       |                (true, std::cmp::Ordering::Equal) => {
 1404|       |                    assert!(matches!(status, ActiveSetRowStatus::ActiveBinding { .. }));
 1405|       |                }
 1406|       |                (false, std::cmp::Ordering::Equal) => {
 1407|       |                    assert!(matches!(status, ActiveSetRowStatus::MissedBindingInequality { .. }));
 1408|       |                }
 1409|       |                (true, std::cmp::Ordering::Less) => {
 1410|       |                    assert!(matches!(status, ActiveSetRowStatus::SuperfluousActiveInequality { .. }));
 1411|       |                }
 1412|       |                (false, std::cmp::Ordering::Less) => {
 1413|       |                    assert!(matches!(status, ActiveSetRowStatus::InactiveStrictlySatisfied { .. }));
 1414|       |                }
 1415|       |            }
 1416|       |        }
 1417|       |

/tmp/hypercurve-closure-prepush-904e/normal/crates/hypersolve/src/algebraic_binary.rs:
    1|       |//! Binary algebraic-number construction for represented real roots.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module constructs the first bounded independent-root arithmetic
    4|       |//! package for `hypersolve`: `gamma = alpha + beta`, `alpha - beta`,
    5|       |//! `alpha * beta`, and guarded `alpha / beta` for two represented real
    6|       |//! algebraic roots.  It uses exact
    7|       |//! resultants to eliminate one source variable, then asks the existing Sturm
    8|       |//! refinement package to certify that the exact image interval contains one
    9|       |//! distinct real root of the resultant. That last step is the important
   10|       |//! boundary: the resultant defines candidate algebraic values, while the
   11|       |//! isolating interval is accepted only after exact replay, not after primitive
   12|       |//! sampling.
   13|       |//!
   14|       |//! The construction combines a Sylvester resultant, Sturm root counting, the
   15|       |//! standard real-root isolation model, and exact replay.
   16|       |
   17|       |use std::borrow::Cow;
   18|       |use std::cmp::Ordering;
   19|       |
   20|       |use hyperlimit::{PredicatePolicy, compare_reals};
   21|       |use hyperreal::Real;
   22|       |
   23|       |use crate::algebraic::{
   24|       |    AlgebraicRootArithmeticOp, AlgebraicRootRepresentation, AlgebraicRootValidationReport,
   25|       |    AlgebraicRootValidationStatus, validate_algebraic_root_representation,
   26|       |};
   27|       |use crate::integer_interpolation::{
   28|       |    interpolate_integer_samples_up_to_scale, primitive_integer_polynomial,
   29|       |};
   30|       |use crate::resultant::resultant_exact_rational_polynomials_value;
   31|       |use crate::root_isolation::{
   32|       |    IsolatedRootInterval, IsolatedRootRefinementStatus, RootIsolationConfig,
   33|       |    refine_isolated_univariate_polynomial_interval, square_free_part,
   34|       |};
   35|       |
   36|       |const MAX_BINARY_RESULTANT_DEGREE: usize = 9;
   37|       |
   38|       |/// Status for constructing a binary arithmetic image of two algebraic roots.
   39|       |#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
   40|       |pub enum AlgebraicRootBinaryTransformStatus {
   41|       |    /// The arithmetic image has exact polynomial and isolating-interval
   42|       |    /// evidence.
   43|       |    Transformed,
   44|       |    /// One or both source roots failed structural validation.
   45|       |    InvalidEvidence,
   46|       |    /// This bounded package does not support the requested arithmetic
   47|       |    /// operation.
   48|       |    UnsupportedOperation,
   49|       |    /// Division was requested, but the divisor interval was not certified
   50|       |    /// away from zero.
   51|       |    DenominatorMayContainZero,
   52|       |    /// The source coefficients are not exact rationals.
   53|       |    UnsupportedCoefficient,
   54|       |    /// The resultant degree exceeds the configured bounded exact package.
   55|       |    UnsupportedDegree,
   56|       |    /// The exact image interval did not certify exactly one resultant root.
   57|       |    NonIsolatingImageInterval,
   58|       |    /// The resultant polynomial or certified interval failed representation
   59|       |    /// validation.
   60|       |    InvalidTransformedEvidence,
   61|       |    /// Exact comparisons, resultant construction, or interpolation did not
   62|       |    /// decide.
   63|       |    Undecided,
   64|       |    /// The enclosing operation declined required promotion or refinement work.
   65|       |    BudgetExhausted,
   66|       |}
   67|       |
   68|       |/// Report for independent-root arithmetic construction.
   69|       |#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
   70|       |pub struct AlgebraicRootBinaryTransformReport {
   71|       |    /// Requested arithmetic operation.
   72|       |    pub operation: AlgebraicRootArithmeticOp,
   73|       |    /// Final construction status.
   74|       |    pub status: AlgebraicRootBinaryTransformStatus,
   75|       |    /// Resulting represented root when construction succeeds or failed
   76|       |    /// validation has useful evidence to inspect.
   77|       |    pub representation: Option<AlgebraicRootRepresentation>,
   78|       |    /// Compact diagnostic reason.
   79|       |    pub message: Option<String>,
   80|       |}
   81|       |
   82|       |/// Construct `alpha (+|-|*|/) beta` as a represented algebraic root.
   83|       |///
   84|       |/// The supported operations are addition, subtraction, multiplication, and
   85|       |/// denominator-certified division.  The defining polynomial is obtained by
   86|       |/// exact univariate resultants:
   87|       |///
   88|       |/// - `alpha + beta`: `Res_x(P(x), Q(y - x))`
   89|       |/// - `alpha - beta`: `Res_x(P(x), Q(x - y))`
   90|       |/// - `alpha * beta`: `Res_x(P(x), x^m Q(y / x))`, where `m = deg(Q)`
   91|       |/// - `alpha / beta`: `Res_x(P(x), y^m Q(x / y))`, after proving `beta != 0`
   92|       |///
   93|       |/// The resultant is sampled at exact integer `y` values and interpolated
   94|       |/// exactly.  This keeps the multivariate polynomial machinery bounded while
   95|       |/// preserving a replayable elimination certificate.  Quotient construction is
   96|       |/// still not a total field API: it refuses divisors whose isolating interval
   97|       |/// may contain zero.

    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! A bivariate subresultant becomes a univariate fiber polynomial after one
    4|       |//! parameter is fixed to an algebraic root. Its coefficients then live in the
    5|       |//! local field at that root, not in `Real`. This module represents those
    6|       |//! coefficients as reduced rational functions of the retained parameter and

 3378|       |/// Projects one bivariate fiber through a degree-bounded algebraic quotient ring.

 5876|      3|    fn diagonal_fiber_deflation_removes_the_exact_local_multiplicity() {
 5877|       |        // F(x, y) = (y - x)^3 (y + 1). At every selected x = alpha the
 5878|       |        // correlated root y = alpha has multiplicity three and leaves y + 1.
 5879|      3|        let polynomial = BivariatePolynomial::new(vec![
 5880|      3|            vec![real(0), real(0), real(0), real(1), real(1)],
 5881|      3|            vec![real(0), real(0), real(-3), real(-3)],

 5884|       |        ]);
 5885|      3|        let expected = BivariatePolynomial::new(vec![vec![real(1), real(1)]]);
 5886|      6|        for policy in [PredicatePolicy::STRICT, PredicatePolicy::APPROXIMATE_512] {
                                    ^3
 5887|      6|            let alpha = represented_root(
 5888|      6|                vec![real(-1), real(0), real(2)],
 5889|      6|                rational(2, 3),

/tmp/hypercurve-closure-prepush-904e/normal/crates/hypersolve/src/algebraic_mobius.rs:
    1|       |//! Linear-fractional construction for represented algebraic roots.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module is a narrow algebraic-construction backend for
    4|       |//! [`crate::AlgebraicRootRepresentation`]. It implements
    5|       |//! `beta = (a * alpha + b) / (c * alpha + d)` by exact polynomial substitution
    6|       |//! and exact interval image construction. It is not a generic algebraic-number
    7|       |//! field: unsupported denominator and invertibility cases remain reportable
    8|       |//! blockers.
    9|       |//!
   10|       |//! The construction follows the exact-object boundary advocated by the exactness boundary:
   11|       |//! coordinates are represented by replayable algebraic evidence, and later
   12|       |//! predicates decide topology from certified reports rather than primitive

/tmp/hypercurve-closure-prepush-904e/normal/crates/hypersolve/src/algebraic_polynomial_image.rs:
    1|       |//! Polynomial-image construction for represented algebraic roots.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module constructs `beta = q(alpha)` for an exact represented root
    4|       |//! `alpha` and an exact-rational polynomial `q`. Unlike affine or Mobius
    5|       |//! images, this needs an elimination step: if `P(alpha)=0`, then `beta` is a
    6|       |//! root of `Res_x(P(x), q(x)-y)`. The implementation keeps the elimination
    7|       |//! polynomial and the mapped isolating interval as replayable evidence.
    8|       |//!
    9|       |//! This is intentionally bounded. A nonzero derivative uses the endpoint-image
   10|       |//! fast path. Stationary or initially nonmonotone maps instead use exact
   11|       |//! interval evaluation and source-root refinement until Bernstein variation
   12|       |//! certifies one distinct resultant root. The univariate resultant is sampled
   13|       |//! at exact integer image values and then interpolated exactly, avoiding
   14|       |//! primitive approximations while reusing the crate's certified machinery.
   15|       |//! It combines a Sylvester resultant with the standard real-root isolation
   16|       |//! model and exact replay.
   17|       |
   18|       |use std::borrow::Cow;
   19|       |use std::cmp::Ordering;
   20|       |
   21|       |use hyperlimit::PredicatePolicy;
   22|       |use hyperreal::{Rational, Real};
   23|       |
   24|       |use crate::algebraic::{
   25|       |    AlgebraicRootRepresentation, AlgebraicRootValidationReport, AlgebraicRootValidationStatus,
   26|       |    validate_algebraic_root_representation,
   27|       |};
   28|       |use crate::algebraic_mobius::{
   29|       |    AlgebraicRootMobiusTransformStatus, transform_algebraic_root_mobius,
   30|       |};
   31|       |use crate::integer_interpolation::{
   32|       |    interpolate_integer_samples_up_to_scale, primitive_integer_polynomial,
   33|       |};
   34|       |use crate::resultant::{
   35|       |    quotient_ring_resultant_polynomial, resultant_exact_rational_polynomials_value,
   36|       |};
   37|       |use crate::root_isolation::{
   38|       |    AlgebraicImageEnclosure, IsolatedRootInterval, certify_algebraic_image_interval,
   39|       |    square_free_part,
   40|       |};
   41|       |
   42|       |const MAX_SYLVESTER_DIMENSION: usize = 8;
   43|       |

    1|       |//! Rational-function images of represented algebraic roots.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module constructs exact evidence for `beta = p(alpha) / q(alpha)`,
    4|       |//! where `alpha` is a represented real algebraic root and `p`, `q` are exact
    5|       |//! polynomials. General exact [`Real`] coefficients are supported for constant
    6|       |//! and linear-fractional maps; nonlinear elimination remains exact-rational
    7|       |//! and bounded. The result is another
    8|       |//! [`crate::AlgebraicRootRepresentation`], not a primitive approximation.
    9|       |//! That distinction is the EGC boundary from the exact-geometric-computation model: construction retains
   10|       |//! exact replayable objects, and later predicates decide signs/topology from
   11|       |//! certificates.
   12|       |//!
   13|       |//! After proving that the authored denominator does not vanish at the selected
   14|       |//! root, the preferred path reduces both map polynomials modulo the defining
   15|       |//! source relation and directly eliminates the source coordinate with
   16|       |//! `Res_x(P(x), p(x) - y*q(x))`.  This is the rational analogue of the
   17|       |//! polynomial-image construction and avoids requiring `p(alpha)` and
   18|       |//! `q(alpha)` to be individually monotone.  If that direct path cannot certify
   19|       |//! a one-root image interval, the implementation falls back to composing the
   20|       |//! already-certified pieces: numerator and denominator polynomial images plus
   21|       |//! the bounded binary quotient package.  Both paths keep domain uncertainty
   22|       |//! report-bearing instead of replacing it with primitive sampling.
   23|       |

  246|       |/// Reusable rational map for several roots of one source polynomial.
  247|       |///
  248|       |/// The exact resultant polynomial of a rational map depends on the source
  249|       |/// polynomial and map coefficients, but not on which real root interval is
  250|       |/// selected. This carrier retains source-modulo map reduction and any remaining
  251|       |/// elimination lazily while every
  252|       |/// [`Self::transform`] call still evaluates the denominator, constructs a
  253|       |/// one-root image interval (refining stationary maps when necessary), and
  254|       |/// validates the represented root independently.

  235|       |        // Keep the root strictly inside the dyadic bracket even when a Real
  236|       |        // witness has a rational value that its normal form did not expose.
  237|  1.47k|        let padding = hyperreal::Rational::from(2_i8)
  238|  1.47k|            .powi(SQRT_WITNESS_INTERVAL_PRECISION.into())
  239|  1.47k|            .ok()?;

  240|  1.47k|        return Some(signed_sqrt_interval_from_positive_bounds(
  241|  1.47k|            nonnegative_dyadic_bound(lower - padding.clone()),
  242|  1.47k|            Real::new(upper + padding),
  243|  1.47k|            branch,
  244|  1.47k|        ));
  245|     25|    }
  246|       |    // Without an exact witness, `represented_root_sign == Greater` proves
  247|       |    // this lower endpoint is nonnegative, including the zero-touching case.
  248|     25|    Some(signed_sqrt_interval_from_positive_bounds(
  249|     25|        source.lower.clone().sqrt().ok()?,
                                                      ^0
  250|     25|        source.upper.clone().sqrt().ok()?,
                                                      ^0
  251|     25|        branch,
  252|       |    ))

  678|       |        fn square_composition_places_every_source_coefficient_exactly(
  679|       |            coefficients in prop::collection::vec(-32_i64..33, 2..20),
  680|       |        ) {

  683|       |            prop_assert_eq!(composed.len(), polynomial.len() * 2 - 1);
  684|       |            for (power, coefficient) in composed.iter().enumerate() {

  693|       |        #[test]
  694|       |        fn exact_rational_source_shortcut_retains_an_independent_unit_isolator(
  695|       |            numerator in 1_i64..64,
  696|       |            denominator in 1_i64..32,
  697|       |        ) {
  698|       |            let source_root = (real(numerator) / real(denominator)).unwrap();
  699|       |            let source = AlgebraicRootRepresentation {
  700|       |                constraint_index: 7,
  701|       |                symbol: SymbolId(3),
  702|       |                interval_index: 2,
  703|       |                polynomial_coefficients: vec![-source_root.clone(), Real::one()],
  704|       |                interval: IsolatedRootInterval {
  705|       |                    lower: source_root.clone(),
  706|       |                    upper: source_root.clone(),
  707|       |                    exact_root: Some(source_root.clone()),
  708|       |                    distinct_root_count: 1,
  709|       |                },
  710|       |                validation: AlgebraicRootValidationReport {
  711|       |                    status: AlgebraicRootValidationStatus::Valid,
  712|       |                    message: None,
  713|       |                },
  714|       |            };
  715|       |            let positive = source_root.sqrt().unwrap();
  716|       |
  717|       |            for branch in [-1, 1] {
  718|       |                let report = square_root_algebraic_root_representation(&source, branch);
  719|       |                prop_assert_eq!(report.status, AlgebraicRootSquareRootStatus::Transformed);
  720|       |                let image = report.representation.unwrap();
  721|       |                prop_assert_eq!(image.constraint_index, source.constraint_index);

    1|       |//! Exact represented images of correlated selected-root tensors.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Binary algebraic arithmetic is useful for genuinely independent values,
    4|       |//! but repeatedly applying it to coordinates that share selected source roots
    5|       |//! loses correlation and multiplies eliminant degrees.  This module keeps the

  127|       |/// Projects the final axis of one selected algebraic tensor after saturating
  128|       |/// target-wide conjugate components.
  129|       |///
  130|       |/// Ordinary sequential norms can be identically zero when *any* foreign
  131|       |/// source tuple makes `relation` vanish for every target value, even though
  132|       |/// the authored selected tuple owns a nonzero polynomial. This construction
  133|       |/// adds a retained tag `z` and eliminates the sum of squares
  134|       |///
  135|       |/// `relation(source, target)^2 + (z - source[0])^2`.

  137|       |/// Every target-wide source component then contributes only retained-axis
  138|       |/// content. Exact polynomial GCD and division remove that content before the
  139|       |/// remaining bivariate relation is projected through the first selected root.

  141|       |/// foreign or complex-source candidates, and callers must replay every root
  142|       |/// against the complete selected tuple. Construction and saturation are
  143|       |/// always `STRICT`; no approximate predicate selects a factor or root.
  144|       |///
  145|       |/// The caller must first prove that the authored selected fiber is not
  146|       |/// identically zero. A zero selected fiber is a component, not a finite root

 1538|      3|    fn translated_quadratic_compaction_preserves_selected_factor_and_ownership() {
 1539|     90|        let q = |n, d| (real(n) / real(d)).unwrap();
                          ^3
 1540|       |        // Four different quadratic factors share a translated center. The
 1541|       |        // original degree-eight eliminant must not follow the selected root
 1542|       |        // into every later tensor product.
 1543|      6|        for center in [q(1, 2), q(-7, 3)] {
                                    ^3
 1544|     36|            let factor = |radius_squared: &Real| {
                              ^6
 1545|     36|                vec![
 1546|     36|                    &center * &center - radius_squared,
 1547|     36|                    real(-2) * &center,
 1548|     36|                    Real::one(),
 1549|       |                ]
 1550|     36|            };
 1551|      6|            let mut polynomial = vec![Real::one()];
 1552|     24|            for radius_squared in [q(3, 16), q(5, 16), q(7, 16), q(11, 16)] {
                                                ^6^6        ^6
 1553|     24|                let next = factor(&radius_squared);
 1554|     24|                let mut product = vec![Real::zero(); polynomial.len() + next.len() - 1];
 1555|     96|                for (i, a) in polynomial.iter().enumerate() {
                                            ^24               ^24
 1556|    288|                    for (j, b) in next.iter().enumerate() {
                                                ^96         ^96
 1557|    288|                        product[i + j] += a * b;
 1558|    288|                    }
 1559|       |                }
 1560|     24|                polynomial = product;
 1561|       |            }
 1562|     12|            for branch in [-1, 1] {
                                        ^6
 1563|     12|                let (lo, hi) = if branch < 0 {
 1564|      6|                    (q(-7, 16), q(-3, 8))
 1565|       |                } else {
 1566|      6|                    (q(3, 8), q(7, 16))
 1567|       |                };
 1568|     12|                let mut root = AlgebraicRootRepresentation {
 1569|     12|                    constraint_index: 7,
 1570|     12|                    symbol: SymbolId(12),
 1571|     12|                    interval_index: usize::from(branch > 0),
 1572|     12|                    polynomial_coefficients: polynomial.clone(),
 1573|     12|                    interval: IsolatedRootInterval {
 1574|     12|                        lower: &center + lo,
 1575|     12|                        upper: &center + hi,
 1576|     12|                        exact_root: None,
 1577|     12|                        distinct_root_count: 1,
 1578|     12|                    },
 1579|     12|                    validation: AlgebraicRootValidationReport {
 1580|     12|                        status: AlgebraicRootValidationStatus::Valid,
 1581|     12|                        message: None,
 1582|     12|                    },
 1583|     12|                };
 1584|     12|                let compact = compact_algebraic_root_low_degree_witness(&root)
 1585|     12|                    .expect("the translated factor must be recovered with exact evidence");
 1586|     12|                assert_eq!(compact.polynomial_coefficients, factor(&q(3, 16)));
 1587|     12|                let witness = &center + real(branch) * q(3, 16).sqrt().unwrap();
 1588|     12|                assert_eq!(compact.exact_point_witness(), Some(&witness));
 1589|     12|                assert_eq!(compact.constraint_index, root.constraint_index);
 1590|     12|                assert_eq!(compact.symbol, root.symbol);
 1591|     12|                assert_eq!(compact.interval_index, root.interval_index);
 1592|     12|                assert_eq!(
 1593|     12|                    validate_algebraic_root_representation(&compact, PredicatePolicy::STRICT)
 1594|       |                        .status,
 1595|       |                    AlgebraicRootValidationStatus::Valid,
 1596|       |                );
 1597|     12|                let mut perturbed = root.clone();
 1598|     12|                perturbed.polynomial_coefficients[0] += q(1, 1_048_576);
 1599|     12|                assert_eq!(
 1600|     12|                    validate_algebraic_root_representation(&perturbed, PredicatePolicy::STRICT)
 1601|       |                        .status,
 1602|       |                    AlgebraicRootValidationStatus::Valid,
 1603|       |                );
 1604|     12|                assert!(compact_algebraic_root_low_degree_witness(&perturbed).is_none());
 1605|       |                // The same root is not owned when it is only the excluded
 1606|       |                // lower endpoint of a non-singleton isolator.
 1607|     12|                root.interval.lower = witness;
 1608|     12|                assert!(compact_algebraic_root_low_degree_witness(&root).is_none());
 1609|       |            }
 1610|       |        }

 1613|     42|    fn sum_relation(count: usize, constant: Real) -> DenseTensorPolynomial {
 1614|     42|        let dimensions = vec![2; count + 1];
 1615|     42|        let mut coefficients = vec![Real::zero(); dimensions.iter().product()];
 1616|     42|        coefficients[0] = -constant;
 1617|     81|        for axis in 0..count {
                                  ^42
 1618|     81|            let mut exponent = vec![0; count + 1];
 1619|     81|            exponent[axis] = 1;
 1620|     81|            coefficients[flat_index(&dimensions, &exponent)] = -Real::one();
 1621|     81|        }
 1622|     42|        let mut exponent = vec![0; count + 1];
 1623|     42|        exponent[count] = 1;
 1624|     42|        coefficients[flat_index(&dimensions, &exponent)] = Real::one();
 1625|     42|        DenseTensorPolynomial::try_new(dimensions, coefficients).unwrap()
 1626|     42|    }

 1628|      3|    fn opposite_conjugate_cubic_fiber_relation() -> DenseTensorPolynomial {
 1629|       |        // (x - y) * (8 t^3 - 1). The selected tuple
 1630|       |        // (sqrt(2), -sqrt(2)) owns one cubic fiber, while the two foreign
 1631|       |        // tuples x=y make the ordinary sequential norm identically zero.
 1632|      3|        let dimensions = vec![2, 2, 4];
 1633|      3|        let mut coefficients = vec![Real::zero(); dimensions.iter().product()];
 1634|     12|        for (exponents, coefficient) in [
 1635|      3|            ([1, 0, 0], real(-1)),
 1636|      3|            ([1, 0, 3], real(8)),
 1637|      3|            ([0, 1, 0], Real::one()),
 1638|      3|            ([0, 1, 3], real(-8)),
 1639|     12|        ] {
 1640|     12|            coefficients[flat_index(&dimensions, &exponents)] = coefficient;
 1641|     12|        }
 1642|      3|        DenseTensorPolynomial::try_new(dimensions, coefficients).unwrap()
 1643|      3|    }

    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module is intentionally narrow. It does not try to make `hypersolve`

/tmp/hypercurve-closure-prepush-904e/normal/crates/hypersolve/src/analysis.rs:
    1|       |//! Solver analysis for repeated residual and Jacobian work.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! The analysis types in this module cache structural facts about constraints
    4|       |//! and residual expressions without evaluating variables or exporting to
    5|       |//! primitive floats. They are advisory scheduling data: a dense f64 linear
    6|       |//! adapter may consume the sparsity map, while a future exact/hyperlattice
    7|       |//! backend can consume the same facts to choose symbolic, affine, sparse, or
    8|       |//! non-polynomial rows. The design follows the exact-geometric-computation
    9|       |//! separation between object structure and arithmetic-package selection; see
   10|       |//! the exact-geometric-computation model.

    1|       |//! Complete finite-fiber topology of a rational plane curve in a rectangle.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Projection includes the discriminant, leading coefficient and both
    4|       |//! horizontal boundaries. Between consecutive events the simple real roots
    5|       |//! are ordered continuous graphs; none can enter or leave the rectangle.
    6|       |//! Every event fiber is isolated independently, including isolated points.
    7|       |//! Adjacency is proved by horizontal separators whose interval evaluations
    8|       |//! exclude zero on the whole connection strip. A numerical trace, a boundary
    9|       |//! seed, or proximity between samples is never a completeness certificate.
   10|       |//!

   12|       |//! intersection multiplicity classifier. The exact defining polynomial is
   13|       |//! retained for those consumers. Vertical components, identically zero

    1|       |//! Exact candidate replay and certification for solver results.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Numeric nonlinear methods are useful proposal engines, but in an exact
    4|       |//! geometry stack the proposed coordinates are not a proof. This module replays
    5|       |//! residuals through analysis exact solver structure and asks `hyperreal` for
    6|       |//! certified signs before accepting or rejecting each row. Combinatorial
    7|       |//! decisions should consume exact or certified information
    8|       |//! or return explicit uncertainty, not primitive-float tolerances. The
    9|       |//! candidate/proof split mirrors the architecture of SolveSpace's symbolic
   10|       |//! residual/Jacobian layer with numerical Newton iteration, but makes the
   11|       |//! post-iteration trust boundary explicit.
   12|       |
   13|       |use hyperlimit::{Certainty, PredicatePolicy, Sign, classify_ball_sign};
   14|       |use hyperreal::{CertifiedRealSign, Real, RealSign, RealSignCertificate};
   15|       |
   16|       |use crate::analysis::ProblemAnalysis;
   17|       |use crate::diagnostics::{ProposalEngineKind, ProposalEnginePrecision, ProposalEngineReport};
   18|       |use crate::eval::EvaluationContext;
   19|       |use crate::model::ConstraintKind;
   20|       |
   21|       |/// Certification policy for replaying one candidate solution.
   22|       |#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
   23|       |pub struct CandidateCertificationConfig {
   24|       |    /// Lowest binary precision allowed for bounded exact-real sign refinement.
   25|       |    ///
   26|       |    /// This is not a tolerance. It is the explicit refinement floor passed to
   27|       |    /// `Real::certified_sign_until` when structural facts alone do not decide a
   28|       |    /// residual sign.
   29|       |    pub min_precision: i32,
   30|       |}
   31|       |
   32|       |impl Default for CandidateCertificationConfig {
   33|  79.4k|    fn default() -> Self {
   34|  79.4k|        Self {
   35|  79.4k|            min_precision: PredicatePolicy::MAX_REFINEMENT_PRECISION,
   36|  79.4k|        }
   37|  79.4k|    }
   38|       |}

   44|       |    CertifiedZero {

   46|       |        certificate: RealSignCertificate,

   49|       |    CertifiedSatisfiedInequality {

   52|       |    },
   53|       |    /// A row was proved violated.
   54|       |    CertifiedViolation {
   55|       |        /// Proven sign of the signed residual after row-kind normalization.
   56|       |        sign: RealSign,

 5620|       |    #[test]
 5621|      3|    fn dense_resultant_preserves_signed_scale_and_repeated_factors() {
 5622|       |        // Res_u(u^n-A(t), u^n-A(t)+Q(t)) = Q(t)^n. Choosing a
 5623|       |        // dense Q=(t-2)^32 exercises packed determinant arithmetic; the
 5624|       |        // binomial theorem independently supplies all output coefficients.
 5625|     18|        let binomial_power = |degree: usize| {
                          ^3
 5626|     18|            let mut choose = num::BigInt::from(1_u8);
 5627|     18|            (0..=degree)
 5628|    882|                .map(|power| {
                               ^18
 5629|    882|                    if power > 0 {
 5630|    864|                        choose = choose.clone() * (degree + 1 - power) / power;
 5631|    864|                    }
                                  ^18
 5632|    882|                    Real::from(Rational::from_bigint(
 5633|    882|                        &choose * num::BigInt::from(-2_i8).pow((degree - power) as u32),
 5634|       |                    ))
 5635|    882|                })
 5636|     18|                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
 5637|     18|        };
 5638|      3|        let first_scale = (real(2) / real(3)).unwrap();
 5639|      3|        let second_scale = (real(-3) / real(5)).unwrap();
 5640|      9|        for degree in 1..=3 {
                                    ^3
 5641|      9|            let mut first = vec![vec![Real::zero(); degree + 1]; 34];
 5642|      9|            first[0][degree] = first_scale.clone();
 5643|      9|            first[33][0] = -first_scale.clone();
 5644|      9|            let mut second = vec![vec![Real::zero(); degree + 1]; 34];
 5645|      9|            second[0][degree] = second_scale.clone();
 5646|      9|            second[33][0] = -second_scale.clone();
 5647|    297|            for (power, coefficient) in binomial_power(32).into_iter().enumerate() {
                                                      ^9                 ^9          ^9
 5648|    297|                second[power][0] = coefficient * &second_scale;
 5649|    297|            }
 5650|      9|            let scale =
 5651|     18|                (0..degree).fold(Real::one(), |value, _| value * &first_scale * &second_scale);
                               ^9         ^9   ^9
 5652|      9|            let expected = binomial_power(32 * degree)
 5653|      9|                .into_iter()
 5654|    585|                .map(|coefficient| coefficient * &scale)
                               ^9
 5655|      9|                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
 5656|      9|            let first = BivariatePolynomial::new(first);
 5657|      9|            let second = BivariatePolynomial::new(second);
 5658|     18|            for (first, second, retained_parameter) in [
 5659|      9|                (
 5660|      9|                    first.clone(),
 5661|      9|                    second.clone(),
 5662|      9|                    CurveResultantParameter::First,
 5663|      9|                ),
 5664|      9|                (
 5665|      9|                    swap_bivariate(&first),
 5666|      9|                    swap_bivariate(&second),
 5667|      9|                    CurveResultantParameter::Second,
 5668|      9|                ),
 5669|      9|            ] {
 5670|     18|                let report = resultant_bivariate_polynomial_system(
 5671|     18|                    &first,
 5672|     18|                    &second,
 5673|     18|                    retained_parameter,
 5674|     18|                    CurveIntersectionResultantConfig {
 5675|     18|                        max_resultant_degree: 66 * degree,
 5676|     18|                        ..CurveIntersectionResultantConfig::default()
 5677|     18|                    },
 5678|       |                );
 5679|     18|                assert_eq!(report.status, CurveIntersectionResultantStatus::Constructed);
 5680|     18|                assert_eq!(report.resultant_coefficients, expected);
 5681|       |            }
 5682|       |        }
 5683|      3|    }

 6992|      3|    fn nonrational_resultant_preserves_specialized_degree_drop_identity() {
 6993|       |        // F(t,u) = (t-1)u^2 + u, G(u) = u-sqrt(2). The generic
 6994|       |        // quadratic/linear resultant is 2(t-1)+sqrt(2). At t=1 the
 6995|       |        // lower-degree resultant has the opposite sign, so interpolating
 6996|       |        // that specialization would produce the wrong polynomial.
 6997|      3|        let alpha = real(2).sqrt().unwrap();
 6998|      3|        let first = BivariatePolynomial::new(vec![
 6999|      3|            vec![real(0), real(1), real(-1)],
 7000|      3|            vec![real(0), real(0), real(1)],
 7001|       |        ]);
 7002|      3|        let second = BivariatePolynomial::new(vec![vec![-alpha.clone(), real(1)]]);
 7003|      6|        for retained in [
 7004|      3|            CurveResultantParameter::First,
 7005|      3|            CurveResultantParameter::Second,
 7006|      3|        ] {
 7007|      6|            let (first, second, orientation) = match retained {
 7008|      3|                CurveResultantParameter::First => (first.clone(), second.clone(), real(1)),
 7009|       |                CurveResultantParameter::Second => {
 7010|      3|                    (swap_bivariate(&first), swap_bivariate(&second), real(-1))
 7011|       |                }
 7012|       |            };
 7013|      6|            let report = resultant_bivariate_polynomial_system(
 7014|      6|                &first,
 7015|      6|                &second,
 7016|      6|                retained,
 7017|      6|                CurveIntersectionResultantConfig::default(),
 7018|       |            );
 7019|      6|            assert_eq!(report.status, CurveIntersectionResultantStatus::Constructed);
 7020|      6|            assert_eq!(report.resultant_coefficients.len(), 2);
 7021|       |            // Compare exact values, including the degree-drop point and
 7022|       |            // points not used by reconstruction. This tests the public
 7023|       |            // polynomial contract without exposing interpolation history.
 7024|     30|            for parameter in [-3, 0, 1, 2, 5].map(real) {
                                           ^6               ^6
 7025|     30|                let expected = &orientation * (real(2) * (&parameter - real(1)) + &alpha);
 7026|     30|                let actual = eval_univariate(&report.resultant_coefficients, &parameter);
 7027|     30|                assert!(matches!(
                                      ^0
 7028|     30|                    (actual - expected).certified_sign_until(-512),
 7029|       |                    CertifiedRealSign::Known {
 7030|       |                        sign: RealSign::Zero,
 7031|       |                        ..
 7032|       |                    }
 7033|       |                ));
 7034|       |            }
 7035|       |        }

 7039|      3|    fn rational_interpolation_preserves_signed_scale_at_degree_drops_on_either_axis() {
 7040|       |        // F=c(t u^7-(t+2)), G=d((t-1)u^6-(t+3)). Coprime exponents
 7041|       |        // give Res(F,G)=c^6 d^7 ((t-1)^7(t+2)^6-t^6(t+3)^7).
 7042|       |        // Dimension 13 uses interpolation; t=0 and t=1 must be skipped as
 7043|       |        // samples without losing their values in the completed polynomial.
 7044|      3|        let c = Real::from(Rational::fraction(2, 3).unwrap());
 7045|      3|        let d = Real::from(Rational::fraction(-5, 7).unwrap());
 7046|      3|        let mut first = vec![vec![real(0); 8]; 2];
 7047|      3|        first[0][0] = -real(2) * &c;
 7048|      3|        first[1][0] = -c.clone();
 7049|      3|        first[1][7] = c.clone();
 7050|      3|        let first = BivariatePolynomial::new(first);
 7051|      3|        let mut second = vec![vec![real(0); 7]; 2];
 7052|      3|        second[0][0] = -real(3) * &d;
 7053|      3|        second[1][0] = -d.clone();
 7054|      3|        second[0][6] = -d.clone();
 7055|      3|        second[1][6] = d.clone();
 7056|      3|        let second = BivariatePolynomial::new(second);
 7057|    462|        let pow = |value: &Real, exponent: usize| {
                          ^3
 7058|  3.00k|            (0..exponent).fold(Real::one(), |result, _| result * value)
                           ^462         ^462 ^462
 7059|    462|        };
 7060|      3|        let scale = pow(&c, 6) * pow(&d, 7);
 7061|      6|        for retained in [
 7062|      3|            CurveResultantParameter::First,
 7063|      3|            CurveResultantParameter::Second,
 7064|      3|        ] {
 7065|      6|            let (first, second, orientation) = match retained {
 7066|      3|                CurveResultantParameter::First => (first.clone(), second.clone(), real(1)),
 7067|       |                CurveResultantParameter::Second => {
 7068|      3|                    (swap_bivariate(&first), swap_bivariate(&second), real(-1))
 7069|       |                }
 7070|       |            };
 7071|      6|            let report = resultant_bivariate_polynomial_system(
 7072|      6|                &first,
 7073|      6|                &second,
 7074|      6|                retained,
 7075|      6|                CurveIntersectionResultantConfig::default(),
 7076|       |            );
 7077|      6|            assert_eq!(report.status, CurveIntersectionResultantStatus::Constructed);
 7078|      6|            assert_eq!(report.degree_bound, 13);
 7079|      6|            assert!(report.resultant_coefficients.len() <= 14);
 7080|       |            // Nineteen independent values determine the entire polynomial
 7081|       |            // of degree at most 13, including both exceptional fibers.
 7082|    114|            for parameter in (-3..=15).map(real) {
                                            ^6       ^6
 7083|    114|                let expected = &orientation
 7084|    114|                    * &scale
 7085|    114|                    * (pow(&(&parameter - real(1)), 7) * pow(&(&parameter + real(2)), 6)
 7086|    114|                        - pow(&parameter, 6) * pow(&(&parameter + real(3)), 7));
 7087|    114|                assert!(eval_univariate(&report.resultant_coefficients, &parameter) == expected);
 7088|       |            }
 7089|       |        }
 7090|      3|    }

 7753|      3|    fn axis_saturation_preserves_rootful_fibers_and_closed_boundaries() {
 7754|      3|        let expected = [
 7755|      3|            BivariatePolynomial::new(vec![vec![real(1), real(1)]]),
 7756|      3|            BivariatePolynomial::new(vec![vec![real(2), real(1)]]),
 7757|      3|        ];
 7758|      3|        let alpha = (real(1) / real(2)).unwrap().sqrt().unwrap();
 7759|     18|        for (constant, slope, rootless) in [
 7760|      3|            (real(2), real(1), true),
 7761|      3|            (alpha.clone(), real(1), true),
 7762|      3|            (-alpha, real(1), false),
 7763|      3|            (real(-1), real(2), false),
 7764|      3|            (real(0), real(1), false),
 7765|      3|            (real(-1), real(1), false),
 7766|      3|        ] {
 7767|     36|            for parameter in [
 7768|     18|                CurveResultantParameter::First,
 7769|     18|                CurveResultantParameter::Second,
 7770|     18|            ] {

 7772|       |                    CurveResultantParameter::First => {
 7773|     18|                        BivariatePolynomial::new(vec![vec![constant.clone()], vec![slope.clone()]])
 7774|       |                    }
 7775|       |                    CurveResultantParameter::Second => {
 7776|     18|                        BivariatePolynomial::new(vec![vec![constant.clone(), slope.clone()]])
 7777|       |                    }

 7779|     36|                let equations = [
 7780|     36|                    multiply_bivariate(&factor, &expected[0]),
 7781|     36|                    multiply_bivariate(&factor, &expected[1]),
 7782|     36|                ];
 7783|     36|                let result =
 7784|     36|                    saturate_rootless_bivariate_axis_factors(&equations, [[&real(0), &real(1)]; 2]);
 7785|     36|                if rootless {
 7786|     12|                    let Classification::Decided(Some(result)) = result else {
 7787|      0|                        panic!("rootless factors may be removed exactly");
 7788|       |                    };
 7789|     24|                    for (actual, expected) in result.iter().zip(&expected) {
                                                            ^12    ^12    ^12 ^12

 7791|     24|                    }
 7792|       |                } else {
 7793|     24|                    assert!(
 7794|     24|                        matches!(result, Classification::Decided(None)),
                                      ^0
 7795|       |                        "a factor root belongs to the closed solution set"
 7796|       |                    );
 7797|       |                }
 7798|       |            }
 7799|       |        }
 7800|      3|        assert_eq!(
 7801|      3|            saturate_rootless_bivariate_axis_factors(&expected, [[&real(0), &real(1)]; 2]),

  248|       |/// Convert a polynomial Bezier control net to exact power basis.
  249|       |///
  250|       |/// For degree `n`, the coefficient of `t^k` is
  251|       |/// `sum_{i=0..k} P_i * binom(n, i) * binom(n-i, k-i) * (-1)^(k-i)`.
  252|       |/// This is just the exact expansion of `P_i * B_i^n(t)`, not a sampled fit.
  253|  2.32k|pub fn substitute_bezier_power_basis(
  254|  2.32k|    control_points: &[PolynomialCurvePoint2],
  255|  2.32k|    config: BezierPowerBasisSubstitutionConfig,
  256|  2.32k|) -> BezierPowerBasisSubstitutionReport {
  257|  2.32k|    if control_points.is_empty() {
  258|      3|        return BezierPowerBasisSubstitutionReport {
  259|      3|            status: BezierPowerBasisSubstitutionStatus::EmptyControlNet,
  260|      3|            degree: None,
  261|      3|            control_points: Vec::new(),
  262|      3|            power_basis: None,
  263|      3|        };
  264|  2.32k|    }
  265|       |
  266|  2.32k|    let degree = control_points.len() - 1;
  267|  2.32k|    if degree > config.max_degree || degree > MAX_INTERNAL_BEZIER_POWER_BASIS_DEGREE {
                                                   ^2.31k
  268|      3|        return BezierPowerBasisSubstitutionReport {
  269|      3|            status: BezierPowerBasisSubstitutionStatus::DegreeExceeded,
  270|      3|            degree: Some(degree),
  271|      3|            control_points: control_points.to_vec(),
  272|      3|            power_basis: None,
  273|      3|        };
  274|  2.31k|    }

  741|  3.14k|        for index in (step..=degree).rev() {

  744|  3.14k|            let denominator = right_knot - left_knot.clone();

  752|       |                }
  753|  3.14k|                CertifiedRealSign::Known { .. } => {}
  754|       |            }

  756|  3.14k|                .map_err(|_| BsplineKnotSpanSubstitutionStatus::DivisionFailed)?;

  768|  1.54k|fn bspline_blossom_homogeneous_point(
  769|  1.54k|    control_points: &[RationalCurveControlPoint2],

  791|  1.57k|            let denominator = right_knot - left_knot.clone();

  821|  4.63k|fn bernstein_scalars_to_power_basis(values: &[Real]) -> Vec<Real> {
  822|  4.63k|    let degree = values.len() - 1;
  823|  4.63k|    let mut coefficients = vec![Real::zero(); degree + 1];
  824|  9.28k|    for (power, coefficient) in coefficients.iter_mut().enumerate().take(degree + 1) {
                                              ^4.63k                  ^4.63k      ^4.63k^4.63k
  825|  13.9k|        for (basis_index, value) in values.iter().enumerate().take(power + 1) {
                                                  ^9.28k ^9.28k ^9.28k      ^9.28k^9.28k
  826|  13.9k|            let mut scale = Real::from(
  827|  13.9k|                (binomial(degree, basis_index)
  828|  13.9k|                    * binomial(degree - basis_index, power - basis_index)) as i64,
  829|       |            );
  830|  13.9k|            if (power - basis_index) % 2 == 1 {
  831|  4.65k|                scale = -scale;
  832|  9.31k|            }
  833|  13.9k|            *coefficient += value.clone() * scale;
  834|       |        }
  835|       |    }
  836|  4.63k|    coefficients
  837|  4.63k|}
  838|       |
  839|  41.9k|fn binomial(n: usize, k: usize) -> u64 {
  840|  41.9k|    if k > n {
  841|      0|        return 0;
  842|  41.9k|    }
  843|  41.9k|    let k = k.min(n - k);
  844|  41.9k|    let mut result = 1u64;
  845|  41.9k|    for index in 1..=k {
                      ^111
  846|    111|        result = result * (n - k + index) as u64 / index as u64;
  847|    111|    }
  848|  41.9k|    result
  849|  41.9k|}

    4|       |/// Numerical proposal engine requested for candidate generation.
    5|       |///
    6|       |/// These engines are not proof systems. They generate candidate coordinates
    7|       |/// that must be replayed through exact residual and predicate certificates
    8|       |/// before acceptance. The list follows the practical geometric-constraint
    9|       |/// solver families exposed by SolveSpace/PlaneGCS and MINPACK: damped

   11|       |/// squares, Powell hybrid, dogleg, BFGS, and SQP.
   12|       |/// the exact-geometric-computation boundary still applies: numerical
   13|       |/// engines propose, exact/certified replay decides.
   14|       |///

   16|       |/// the Levenberg-Marquardt method, for the damped least-squares proposal family; and
   17|       |/// the Powell hybrid method, for dogleg-style

    1|       |//! Candidate-domain certification for residual expressions.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Exact replay should fail loudly when a candidate leaves the mathematical
    4|       |//! domain of a residual, but callers often need that information before asking
    5|       |//! for a scalar value. This module walks residual expression trees and reports
    6|       |//! proof-bearing domain checks for division, negative powers, square roots,
    7|       |//! logarithms, inverse circular functions, and inverse hyperbolic functions.
    8|       |//! The checks use exact `Real` comparisons through `hyperlimit`, preserving
    9|       |//! the rule that decisions consume certified facts or return
   10|       |//! explicit uncertainty. The interval/domain separation also follows Moore's
   11|       |//! interval-analysis discipline: domain validity is a precondition
   12|       |//! certificate, not a residual tolerance.
   13|       |
   14|       |use std::cmp::Ordering;
   15|       |
   16|       |use hyperlimit::{PredicatePolicy, compare_reals};
   17|       |use hyperreal::Real;
   18|       |
   19|       |use crate::eval::EvaluationContext;
   20|       |use crate::model::Problem;
   21|       |use crate::symbolic::{Expr, ExprEvalError, SymbolId};
   22|       |
   23|       |/// Mathematical-domain condition checked for one expression node.
   24|       |#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
   25|       |pub enum DomainCheckKind {
   26|       |    /// Denominator of `left / right` must be nonzero.
   27|       |    DivisionDenominatorNonZero,
   28|       |    /// Base of `base.powi(exponent)` must be nonzero when `exponent < 0`.
   29|       |    NegativePowerBaseNonZero,
   30|       |    /// Base of `base.powi(0)` must be nonzero because Hyperreal leaves `0^0`
   31|       |    /// undefined.
   32|       |    ZeroPowerBaseNonZero,
   33|       |    /// Operand of `sqrt(value)` must be nonnegative.
   34|       |    SqrtOperandNonNegative,
   35|       |    /// Operand of `log10(value)` must be strictly positive.
   36|       |    Log10OperandPositive,
   37|       |    /// Operand of `ln(value)` must be strictly positive.
   38|       |    LnOperandPositive,
   39|       |    /// Operand of `asin(value)` must lie in the closed interval `[-1, 1]`.

    1|       |//! Exact failed-constraint and redundancy diagnostics.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Candidate certification answers whether each active residual row is
    4|       |//! satisfied, violated, unknown, or domain-failed. CAD/sketch solver APIs also
    5|       |//! need a source-row diagnostic list for failed-constraint displays and
    6|       |//! SolveSpace-style status reporting. This module builds that list without
    7|       |//! introducing tolerances: it combines exact residual replay with exact affine
    8|       |//! rank checks. That follows the exact-geometric-computation boundary:
    9|       |//! numerical iteration may propose a candidate, but failure explanations must
   10|       |//! be certified or explicitly undecided. The rank
   11|       |//! redundancy test uses Bareiss-backed affine rank reports; see fraction-free elimination.
   12|       |
   13|       |use crate::analysis::ProblemAnalysis;
   14|       |use crate::certification::{
   15|       |    CandidateCertificationConfig, CandidateCertificationReport, CertifiedCandidateRow,
   16|       |    CertifiedCandidateStatus, certify_candidate_with_config,
   17|       |};
   18|       |use crate::eval::EvaluationContext;
   19|       |use crate::model::ConstraintKind;
   20|       |use crate::rank::{ExactAffineRankReport, ExactAffineRankStatus, analyze_exact_affine_rank};
   21|       |
   22|       |/// Per-source-row diagnostic status for failed-constraint reporting.
   23|       |#[derive(Clone, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
   24|       |pub enum FailedConstraintStatus {
   25|       |    /// A structurally constant active row was proved impossible.
   26|       |    ///
   27|       |    /// For equality-like rows this means a nonzero constant residual. For
   28|       |    /// inequalities this means a constant signed residual that violates the
   29|       |    /// normalized inequality. It is a model contradiction, not merely a bad
   30|       |    /// candidate.
   31|       |    CertifiedContradiction,
   32|       |    /// The current candidate was proved to violate this row, but the row is
   33|       |    /// not structurally constant.
   34|       |    CertifiedCandidateViolation,
   35|       |    /// The row is exactly rank-redundant in the active affine equality system.
   36|       |    RankRedundant,
   37|       |    /// The row only carries lossy proposal evidence; exact replay has not been
   38|       |    /// performed for it.
   39|       |    DidNotConvergeOnly,
   40|       |    /// Exact replay hit a domain/evaluation failure.
   41|       |    DomainFailure,
   42|       |    /// Exact replay completed but bounded sign refinement did not decide.
   43|       |    BoundedUnknown,
   44|       |}
   45|       |

    1|       |//! Interval-box certification for solver candidates.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module is the first variable-box proof stage for `hypersolve`. For an
    4|       |//! affine residual `c + a*x + b*y`, a box around the candidate maps to an exact
    5|       |//! residual ball with radius `|a|*rx + |b|*ry`. For quadratic row forms,
    6|       |//! the same proof stage uses exact Taylor enclosures: univariate
    7|       |//! `|(2*a*x0 + b)|*r + |a|*r^2`, and multivariate
    8|       |//! `sum_i |grad_i(x0)|*r_i + sum_ij |q_ij|*r_i*r_j`. The final sign proof is
    9|       |//! delegated to `hyperlimit`'s certified ball filter, keeping this layer inside the exact
   10|       |//! proof-producing filter model rather than turning solver tolerances into
   11|       |//! topology. The interval-box shape follows Moore's interval-analysis
   12|       |//! tradition and the Taylor-model/Krawczyk validation lineage, while the

                          ^6      ^6                       ^6

                                          ^6

 1113|     12|                shifted[0] += Real::from(residual);

  370|       |/// Replays a candidate solution through sparse exact residuals.
  371|       |///
  372|       |/// The declared shape is validated before any proof decision is made. Sparse
  373|       |/// terms are then accumulated exactly into `row_count` residual slots, the
  374|       |/// right-hand side is subtracted, and each residual sign first uses
  375|       |/// `Real::certified_sign_until`, then the strict exact predicate cascade if the
  376|       |/// caller's refinement bound is exhausted. This keeps sparse numeric solvers, fill
  377|       |/// reducers, and domain-specific stamp assemblers outside the proof boundary:
  378|       |/// they may propose `x`, but this replay report decides whether `A*x-b` is
  379|       |/// actually zero. This is the same construction/proof separation emphasized by
  380|       |/// the exact-geometric-computation model.

  389|  3.11k|    SparseLinearSystem::from_terms(row_count, column_count, terms, rhs)?
                                                                                     ^9
  390|  3.10k|        .replay_candidate(candidate, min_precision)
  391|  3.11k|}

  690|       |///
  691|       |/// This is the low-level refinement hook for represented algebraic numbers.
  692|       |/// It does not approximate a root. It validates an exact coefficient-field

  694|       |/// unique root, and otherwise removes repeated factors with a polynomial gcd
  695|       |/// and verifies the supplied partition-owned `(lower, upper]` interval with a
  696|       |/// Sturm count. It then repeatedly bisects the proved one-root interval. Any
  697|       |/// supplied exact witness is checked for closed containment, vanishing, and
  698|       |/// interval uniqueness before it is accepted.

  700|       |/// model; exact refinement remains the design rule used here.
  701|  10.4k|pub fn refine_isolated_univariate_polynomial_interval(
  702|  10.4k|    polynomial: &[Real],
  703|  10.4k|    interval: &IsolatedRootInterval,
  704|  10.4k|    config: RootIsolationConfig,
  705|  10.4k|) -> IsolatedRootRefinementReport {
  706|  10.4k|    let policy = config.policy;

 2122|       |/// Return a rational power-of-two instance of Fujiwara's real-root bound.
 2123|       |///
 2124|       |/// For `p(x) = a_n x^n + ... + a_0`, put
 2125|       |/// `M = max_i |a_i/a_n|^(1/(n-i))`.  If `|x| > 2M`, the lower terms divided
 2126|       |/// by the leading term are bounded by a strict geometric series with ratio
 2127|       |/// one half, so `p(x)` cannot be zero.  Each radical is rounded upward to a
 2128|       |/// power of two using exact numerator/denominator product bit lengths.  The
 2129|       |/// resulting endpoint is exact, cheap for the dyadic scalar kernels, and much

 3689|      3|            &sum * &sum - (real(5) + real(2) * real(6).sqrt().expect("positive square root"));
 3690|      3|        assert!(!radical_zero.definitely_zero());

 3794|      3|    fn fraction_free_bernstein_exceeds_machine_binomial_range_exactly() {
 3795|       |        // (x - 1/2)(x + 1)^79 has exactly one root in (2/5, 3/5). Degree 80
 3796|       |        // makes its central binomial coefficient larger than u64, exercising
 3797|       |        // the fraction-free falling-factorial basis conversion directly.
 3798|      3|        let mut repeated_factor = vec![Real::one()];
 3799|      3|        for _ in 0..79 {
 3800|    237|            let mut next = vec![Real::zero(); repeated_factor.len() + 1];
 3801|  9.48k|            for (index, coefficient) in repeated_factor.iter().enumerate() {
                                                      ^237                   ^237
 3802|  9.48k|                next[index] += coefficient.clone();
 3803|  9.48k|                next[index + 1] += coefficient.clone();
 3804|  9.48k|            }
 3805|    237|            repeated_factor = next;
 3806|       |        }
 3807|      3|        let half = (real(1) / real(2)).unwrap();
 3808|      3|        let mut polynomial = vec![Real::zero(); repeated_factor.len() + 1];
 3809|    240|        for (index, coefficient) in repeated_factor.iter().enumerate() {
                                                  ^3                     ^3
 3810|    240|            polynomial[index] -= half.clone() * coefficient.clone();
 3811|    240|            polynomial[index + 1] += coefficient.clone();
 3812|    240|        }
 3813|       |
 3814|      3|        assert_eq!(
 3815|      3|            exact_rational_polynomial_interval_bernstein_variations(
 3816|      3|                &polynomial,
 3817|      3|                &(real(2) / real(5)).unwrap(),
 3818|      3|                &(real(3) / real(5)).unwrap(),
 3819|       |            ),

 4146|       |        #[test]
 4147|       |        fn generated_interval_presence_helpers_match_distinct_root_sets(
 4148|       |            roots in prop::collection::vec(-5_i8..=5, 1..=7),
 4149|       |            first_bound in -6_i8..=6,
 4150|       |            second_bound in -6_i8..=6,
 4151|       |            denominator in 1_u8..=5,
 4152|       |        ) {
 4153|       |            let mut polynomial = vec![Real::one()];
 4154|       |            for root in &roots {
 4155|       |                let root = Real::from(
 4156|       |                    HyperRational::fraction(i64::from(*root), u64::from(denominator))
 4157|       |                        .expect("generated denominator is positive"),
 4158|       |                );
 4159|       |                let mut next = vec![Real::zero(); polynomial.len() + 1];
 4160|       |                for (index, coefficient) in polynomial.iter().enumerate() {
 4161|       |                    next[index] -= coefficient * &root;
 4162|       |                    next[index + 1] += coefficient;
 4163|       |                }
 4164|       |                polynomial = next;
 4165|       |            }
 4166|       |            let mut distinct_roots = roots;
 4167|       |            distinct_roots.sort_unstable();
 4168|       |            distinct_roots.dedup();
 4169|       |            let (lower, upper) = if first_bound <= second_bound {
 4170|       |                (first_bound, second_bound)
 4171|       |            } else {
 4172|       |                (second_bound, first_bound)
 4173|       |            };
 4174|       |            let expected_open = lower < upper
 4175|       |                && distinct_roots
 4176|       |                    .iter()
 4177|  2.43k|                    .filter(|root| lower < **root && **root < upper)
                                                                   ^1.52k
 4178|       |                    .count()
 4179|       |                    == 1;
 4180|       |            let expected_half_open = lower < upper
 4181|       |                && distinct_roots
 4182|       |                    .iter()
 4183|  2.43k|                    .filter(|root| lower < **root && **root <= upper)
                                                                   ^1.52k
 4184|       |                    .count()
 4185|       |                    == 1;
 4186|       |            let expected_closed_empty = distinct_roots
 4187|       |                .iter()
 4188|  1.60k|                .all(|root| *root < lower || upper < *root);
                                                           ^804
 4189|       |            let lower = Real::from(
 4190|       |                HyperRational::fraction(i64::from(lower), u64::from(denominator))
 4191|       |                    .expect("generated denominator is positive"),
 4192|       |            );
 4193|       |            let upper = Real::from(
 4194|       |                HyperRational::fraction(i64::from(upper), u64::from(denominator))
 4195|       |                    .expect("generated denominator is positive"),
 4196|       |            );
 4197|       |
 4198|       |            prop_assert_eq!(
 4199|       |                polynomial_has_one_distinct_root_in_open_interval(
 4200|       |                    &polynomial,
 4201|       |                    &lower,
 4202|       |                    &upper,
 4203|       |                    PredicatePolicy::STRICT,
 4204|       |                ),
 4205|       |                Some(expected_open)
 4206|       |            );
 4207|       |            prop_assert_eq!(
 4208|       |                polynomial_has_one_distinct_root_with_ownership(
 4209|       |                    &polynomial,
 4210|       |                    &lower,
 4211|       |                    &upper,
 4212|       |                    PredicatePolicy::STRICT,
 4213|       |                    false, true,
 4214|       |                ),
 4215|       |                Some(expected_half_open)
 4216|       |            );
 4217|       |            prop_assert_eq!(
 4218|       |                polynomial_has_no_distinct_root_in_closed_interval(

 4220|       |                    &lower,
 4221|       |                    &upper,

 5017|       |    // Closed-form boundary sums provide an oracle independent of the
 5018|       |    // adjacent-sum/de Casteljau implementation being tested.
 5019|    648|    fn binomial_midpoint_controls(
 5020|    648|        coefficients: &[num::BigRational],
 5021|    648|    ) -> (Vec<num::BigRational>, Vec<num::BigRational>) {
 5022|   326k|        let binomial = |n: usize, k: usize| {
                          ^648
 5023|   326k|            let mut value = BigInt::one();
 5024|  5.71M|            for i in 0..k {
                                   ^326k
 5025|  5.71M|                value *= n - i;
 5026|  5.71M|                value /= i + 1;
 5027|  5.71M|            }
 5028|   326k|            value
 5029|   326k|        };
 5030|    648|        let n = coefficients.len() - 1;
 5031|    648|        let left = (0..=n)
 5032|  8.64k|            .map(|j| {
                           ^648
 5033|  8.64k|                (0..=j)
 5034|   163k|                    .map(|k| &coefficients[k] * binomial(j, k))
                                   ^8.64k
 5035|  8.64k|                    .sum::<num::BigRational>()
 5036|  8.64k|                    / (BigInt::one() << j)
 5037|  8.64k|            })
 5038|    648|            .collect();
 5039|    648|        let right = (0..=n)
 5040|  8.64k|            .map(|j| {
                           ^648
 5041|  8.64k|                (0..=n - j)
 5042|   163k|                    .map(|k| &coefficients[j + k] * binomial(n - j, k))
                                   ^8.64k
 5043|  8.64k|                    .sum::<num::BigRational>()
 5044|  8.64k|                    / (BigInt::one() << (n - j))
 5045|  8.64k|            })
 5046|    648|            .collect();
 5047|    648|        (left, right)
 5048|    648|    }

   26|       |/// equation and isolator supply the Sturm-Tarski proof. A fully evaluated
   27|       |/// tensor uses a STRICT scalar sign. More unresolved axes or unavailable exact
   28|       |/// decisions return `None`; callers retain the original tuple for other proofs.
   29|       |/// No defining equation, selected root, or interval is replaced in the caller.

   63|       |/// Signs a polynomial at a caller-certified singleton over an exact ordered field.
   64|       |///
   65|       |/// Coefficients are in ascending power order. `defining` must have exactly one
   66|       |/// distinct root in the supplied interval; selection and coefficient-field
   67|       |/// identity remain owned by the caller. Repeated roots are allowed. Endpoint
   68|       |/// roots, point intervals and invalid interval metadata return `None`.
   69|       |///
   70|       |/// The division-free Sturm-Tarski chain uses only the existing field
   71|       |/// arithmetic and exact signs. Positive pseudo-remainder scales preserve the
   72|       |/// query's sign, including for nonmonic and negative leading coefficients.
   73|       |/// The field removes available common positive content before it compounds
   74|       |/// through later remainders, preserving the caller's original root authority.
   75|       |/// Only two successive polynomials are retained; no root refinement, field
   76|       |/// projection or independent root isolation is required. Unavailable field
   77|       |/// decisions propagate through the context's error type.
   78|    900|pub fn ordered_field_sign_at_selected_root<C: Clone, F: OrderedFieldPolynomialContext<C>>(

  494|       |/// Retained high-level sketch constraint families.
  495|       |#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
  496|       |pub enum SketchConstraintKind {
  497|       |    /// Coincident 2D or 3D points.
  498|       |    PointsCoincident {
  499|       |        /// First point entity.
  500|       |        a: SketchEntityHandle,
  501|       |        /// Second point entity.
  502|       |        b: SketchEntityHandle,
  503|       |    },
  504|       |    /// Point-to-point squared-distance constraint.
  505|       |    PointPointDistance {
  506|       |        /// First point entity.
  507|       |        a: SketchEntityHandle,
  508|       |        /// Second point entity.
  509|       |        b: SketchEntityHandle,
  510|       |        /// Distance entity.
  511|       |        distance: SketchEntityHandle,
  512|       |    },
  513|       |    /// Point-to-point bounded-distance relation.
  514|       |    ///
  515|       |    /// Bounds are exact distance values. Lowering uses squared-distance
  516|       |    /// inequalities only after proving that the bounds are nonnegative, so a
  517|       |    /// negative upper bound cannot be accidentally accepted by squaring. This
  518|       |    /// follows the exact-geometric-computation boundary advocated by the exact-geometric-computation model: retain the semantic
  519|       |    /// object, then lower only to certified exact predicates.
  520|       |    PointPointDistanceRange {
  521|       |        /// First point entity.
  522|       |        a: SketchEntityHandle,
  523|       |        /// Second point entity.
  524|       |        b: SketchEntityHandle,
  525|       |        /// Optional exact lower distance bound.
  526|       |        lower: Option<Real>,
  527|       |        /// Optional exact upper distance bound.
  528|       |        upper: Option<Real>,
  529|       |    },
  530|       |    /// Bounded point-to-point distance after projection into a workplane.
  531|       |    ///
  532|       |    /// Bounds are exact distance values in the retained workplane metric.
  533|       |    /// Lowering first validates that the lower and upper bounds are
  534|       |    /// nonnegative and ordered, then emits the workplane unit-quaternion guard
  535|       |    /// and squared projected-distance inequalities. This is the range
  536|       |    /// counterpart of [`SketchConstraintKind::ProjectedPointPointDistance`].
  537|       |    /// It follows the exact-geometric-computation model by
  538|       |    /// keeping invalid semantic bounds as diagnostics instead of accepting
  539|       |    /// misleading squared rows. The retained frame uses the unit-quaternion construction's
  540|       |    /// unit-quaternion rotation matrix.
  541|       |    ProjectedPointPointDistanceRange {
  542|       |        /// Workplane entity that supplies origin and normal/quaternion.
  543|       |        workplane: SketchEntityHandle,
  544|       |        /// First 3D point entity.
  545|       |        a: SketchEntityHandle,
  546|       |        /// Second 3D point entity.
  547|       |        b: SketchEntityHandle,
  548|       |        /// Optional exact lower projected distance bound.
  549|       |        lower: Option<Real>,
  550|       |        /// Optional exact upper projected distance bound.
  551|       |        upper: Option<Real>,
  552|       |    },
  553|       |    /// Point-to-point distance after orthogonal projection into a workplane.
  554|       |    ///
  555|       |    /// The retained relation is SolveSpace-style projected distance: two 3D
  556|       |    /// points are interpreted through a retained workplane and only their
  557|       |    /// `U/V` displacement is compared to the exact distance carrier. Lowering
  558|       |    /// emits a unit-quaternion guard for the workplane plus
  559|       |    /// `(delta . U)^2 + (delta . V)^2 - d^2 == 0`. The guard is part of the
  560|       |    /// generated proof package because the polynomial projection is valid only
  561|       |    /// for a certified unit frame. This does so by keeping projection as retained object
  562|       |    /// structure and accepting candidates only through exact residual replay.
  563|       |    /// The exact `U/V/N` axes use the standard unit-quaternion rotation matrix;
  564|       |    /// see the unit-quaternion construction.
  565|       |    ProjectedPointPointDistance {
  566|       |        /// Workplane entity that supplies origin and normal/quaternion.
  567|       |        workplane: SketchEntityHandle,
  568|       |        /// First 3D point entity.
  569|       |        a: SketchEntityHandle,
  570|       |        /// Second 3D point entity.
  571|       |        b: SketchEntityHandle,
  572|       |        /// Distance entity.
  573|       |        distance: SketchEntityHandle,
  574|       |    },
  575|       |    /// Projected 3D point-pair distance equal to a retained circle/arc radius.
  576|       |    ///
  577|       |    /// Lowering projects the retained 3D point-pair displacement into a
  578|       |    /// certified workplane frame and emits `|a-b|_uv^2 - radius^2 == 0`.
  579|       |    /// This keeps the point-pair distance relation explicit instead of
  580|       |    /// forcing callers to introduce a helper line segment or trust rounded
  581|       |    /// projected coordinates. The exact-geometric-computation model supplies the exact replay boundary; the unit-quaternion construction supplies the unit-quaternion
  582|       |    /// frame, and the geometric-constraint-solver model,
  583|       |    /// motivates retaining the radius-equality relation as source evidence.
  584|       |    ProjectedPointRadiusEquality3 {
  585|       |        /// Workplane entity that supplies origin and normal/quaternion.
  586|       |        workplane: SketchEntityHandle,
  587|       |        /// First 3D point of the projected distance.
  588|       |        a: SketchEntityHandle,
