 1867|       |    /// Lowering first proves the workplane unit-quaternion guard, projects the
 1868|       |    /// retained 3D point relative to the workplane origin into exact `U/V`
 1869|       |    /// coordinates, then replays the ordinary Bernstein-coordinate equations
 1870|       |    /// `point_uv.axis - B_axis(t) == 0` against a retained 2D cubic Bezier.
 1871|       |    /// The parameter is retained as source data; segment-domain policy remains
 1872|       |    /// an explicit [`SketchParameterDomain::Bounded`] or range obligation.
 1873|       |    /// This follows the exact-geometric-computation model: the
 1874|       |    /// projection frame, curve, and parameter are preserved, while exact
 1875|       |    /// residual replay accepts candidates. The workplane frame follows
 1876|       |    /// the unit-quaternion construction, and the
 1877|       |    /// Bernstein/de Casteljau curve model follows the Bernstein/de Casteljau construction.
 1878|       |    ProjectedPointOnCubic3 {
 1879|       |        /// Workplane entity that supplies origin and normal/quaternion.
 1880|       |        workplane: SketchEntityHandle,
 1881|       |        /// 3D point constrained to the projected curve point.
 1882|       |        point: SketchEntityHandle,
 1883|       |        /// Retained 2D cubic Bezier entity in workplane coordinates.
 1884|       |        cubic: SketchEntityHandle,
 1885|       |        /// Curve parameter used by the incidence equations.
 1886|       |        parameter: SketchParameterHandle,
 1887|       |    },
 1888|       |    /// 3D/workplane point-on-3D-cubic-Bezier incidence at a retained parameter.
 1889|       |    ///
 1890|       |    /// Lowering first proves the workplane unit-quaternion guard, projects the
 1891|       |    /// retained 3D point and all four retained 3D cubic control points relative
 1892|       |    /// to the workplane origin, evaluates the projected cubic in exact
 1893|       |    /// Bernstein form, then replays `point_uv.axis - B_uv.axis(t) == 0`.
 1894|       |    /// The curve remains a 3D source object; the workplane projection is part
 1895|       |    /// of the proof package rather than a lossy preprocessing step. This is
 1896|       |    /// the exact-object/replay boundary advocated by the exact-geometric-computation model. The frame uses the unit-quaternion construction's unit
 1897|       |    /// quaternion rotation matrix from the unit-quaternion construction, and the cubic evaluation follows the
 1898|       |    /// Bernstein/de Casteljau model in the Bernstein/de Casteljau construction.
 1899|       |    ProjectedPointOnCubicCurve3 {
 1900|       |        /// Workplane entity that supplies origin and normal/quaternion.
 1901|       |        workplane: SketchEntityHandle,
 1902|       |        /// 3D point constrained to the projected curve point.
 1903|       |        point: SketchEntityHandle,
 1904|       |        /// Retained 3D cubic Bezier entity.
 1905|       |        cubic: SketchEntityHandle,
 1906|       |        /// Curve parameter used by the incidence equations.
 1907|       |        parameter: SketchParameterHandle,
 1908|       |    },
 1909|       |    /// Scalar parameter range constraint.
 1910|       |    ParameterRange {
 1911|       |        /// Parameter constrained by the range.
 1912|       |        parameter: SketchParameterHandle,
 1913|       |        /// Optional exact lower bound.
 1914|       |        lower: Option<Real>,
 1915|       |        /// Optional exact upper bound.
 1916|       |        upper: Option<Real>,
 1917|       |    },
 1918|       |    /// Nondecreasing relation between two scalar parameters.
 1919|       |    ///
 1920|       |    /// Lowering emits `upper - lower >= 0` as an exact inequality row. This is
 1921|       |    /// the generic monotonicity primitive for sketch parameters; domain-specific
 1922|       |    /// clearance or manufacturing interpretations should retain their own
 1923|       |    /// source objects and feed this only as a scalar proof obligation.
 1924|       |    ParameterOrdering {
 1925|       |        /// Parameter that must not exceed `upper`.
 1926|       |        lower: SketchParameterHandle,
 1927|       |        /// Parameter that must be greater than or equal to `lower`.
 1928|       |        upper: SketchParameterHandle,
 1929|       |    },
 1930|       |    /// Minimum exact separation between two ordered scalar parameters.
 1931|       |    ///
 1932|       |    /// Lowering emits `upper - lower - margin >= 0` after proving `margin` is
 1933|       |    /// nonnegative. This is the generic sketch-level design-rule-margin
 1934|       |    /// primitive; domain crates should still own fabrication-specific rule
 1935|       |    /// names, units, and geometry.
 1936|       |    ParameterMargin {
 1937|       |        /// Lower-side parameter.
 1938|       |        lower: SketchParameterHandle,
 1939|       |        /// Upper-side parameter.
 1940|       |        upper: SketchParameterHandle,
 1941|       |        /// Required exact nonnegative margin.
 1942|       |        margin: Real,
 1943|       |    },
 1944|       |    /// Soft objective that keeps a parameter near a target value.
 1945|       |    StayNearParameter {
 1946|       |        /// Parameter to bias.
 1947|       |        parameter: SketchParameterHandle,
 1948|       |        /// Exact target value.
 1949|       |        target: Real,
 1950|       |        /// Exact objective row weight.
 1951|       |        weight: Real,
 1952|       |    },
 1953|       |}

 4194|       |    /// The returned [`SketchLoweringReport`] is deliberately report-bearing:

 4205|   885k|                variable.fixed = parameter.fixed;
 4206|   885k|            }

 4207|       |        }
 4208|       |

                                        ^60.5k

 4217|       |    ///

    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! A point lying on the parent circle is not enough to prove point-on-arc

    1|       |//! Exact retained circular-arc length packages for sketch constraints.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Circular arc length is not a polynomial predicate in the general retained
    4|       |//! endpoint model: it is `r * theta`, and `theta` is recovered from the
    5|       |//! endpoint radius vectors. Following the exact-geometric-computation model, this module keeps that
    6|       |//! semantic boundary explicit instead of disguising the relation as an
    7|       |//! algebraic row. The endpoint-on-radius equations remain polynomial proof
    8|       |//! obligations, while the line/arc length equality is retained as an exact
    9|       |//! symbolic transcendental residual. The decomposition matches the
   10|       |//! constraint-solver modeling split used by geometric constraint solvers: construction objects are retained, and replay checks the exact rows
   11|       |//! appropriate to each object.
   12|       |
   13|       |use hyperreal::Real;
   14|       |
   15|       |use crate::symbolic::Expr;
   16|       |
   17|       |/// Exact residual expressions for a retained 2D line/minor-arc length relation.
   18|       |#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
   19|       |pub(crate) struct LineArcLengthExprs {

   21|       |    /// radius circle.

   23|       |    /// Exact symbolic residual `|line|^2 - (radius * acos(cos(theta)))^2`.
   24|       |    ///
   25|       |    /// The angle is the principal unsigned angle between the retained start
   26|       |    /// and end radius vectors, so this is the minor arc length in `[0, pi]`.
   27|       |    /// Major or oriented arc lengths require an explicit branch carrier and
   28|       |    /// are intentionally not inferred from floating sweep data.

   30|       |}

   46|       |/// Build exact rows for a retained line length equal to a circular minor arc.
   47|       |///
   48|       |/// Let `s = start - center`, `e = end - center`, and `d` be the line direction.
   49|       |/// The package contains:
   50|       |///
   51|       |/// - `|s|^2 - radius^2 == 0`;
   52|       |/// - `|e|^2 - radius^2 == 0`;
   53|       |/// - `|d|^2 - (radius * acos((s . e) / (|s| |e|)))^2 == 0`.
   54|       |///

   56|       |/// it through `hyperreal`, but callers should not treat it as a polynomial
   57|       |/// proof row. The line length is squared to avoid introducing a second
   58|       |/// square-root branch for a segment whose length is already nonnegative by
   59|       |/// construction. Zero-radius arcs and degenerate endpoints remain explicit
   60|       |/// retained-domain obligations because the cosine expression divides by

   72|  1.58k|    ];

   75|  1.58k|        end[1].clone() - center[1].clone(),
   76|  1.58k|    ];

   78|  1.58k|    let arc_length = radius.clone() * cosine.acos();

   89|       |/// Build exact rows for a retained line length equal to an explicit circular
   90|       |/// sweep branch.
   91|       |///
   92|       |/// `theta = acos(cos(s,e))` is the principal unsigned endpoint angle. The
   93|       |/// retained [`SketchArcLengthSweep`] chooses both a direction and whether that
   94|       |/// direction follows the minor or major sweep:
   95|       |///
   96|       |/// - counterclockwise minor: `s x e >= 0`, angle `theta`;
   97|       |/// - clockwise minor: `-(s x e) >= 0`, angle `theta`;
   98|       |/// - counterclockwise major: `-(s x e) >= 0`, angle `2*pi - theta`;
   99|       |/// - clockwise major: `s x e >= 0`, angle `2*pi - theta`.
  100|       |///
  101|       |/// The signed branch row is not redundant metadata. It is the exact replay

    1|       |//! Sketch construction certificate manifests.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Downstream geometry and simulation crates should not have to infer whether a
    4|       |//! solved sketch is trustworthy from primitive coordinates alone. This module

    1|       |//! Exact circle/circle tangency packages for retained sketch constraints.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! The sketch layer resolves circle handles, radius handles, and branch flags;
    4|       |//! this module owns only the symbolic proof rows. This is the retained-object
    5|       |//! split advocated by the exact-geometric-computation model: a caller chooses the topological
    6|       |//! tangency branch, and exact replay accepts or rejects the polynomial
    7|       |//! evidence. The branch vocabulary mirrors the explicit geometric-constraint
    8|       |//! solver objects described by the geometric-constraint literature,
    9|       |//! the geometric-constraint-solver model.
   10|       |
   11|       |use crate::symbolic::Expr;
   12|       |
   13|       |/// Exact residual expressions for retained 2D circle/circle tangency.
   14|       |#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
   15|       |pub(crate) struct CircleCircleTangentExprs {
   16|       |    /// Branch-specific polynomial row:
   17|       |    /// `|center_b-center_a|^2 - (r_a+r_b)^2` for external tangency, or
   18|       |    /// `|center_b-center_a|^2 - (r_a-r_b)^2` for internal tangency.
   19|       |    pub(crate) tangency: Expr,
   20|       |}
   21|       |
   22|       |/// Build the exact circle/circle tangency row for a retained branch.
   23|       |///
   24|       |/// Let `d = center_b - center_a`. External tangency replays
   25|       |/// `|d|^2 == (r_a + r_b)^2`; internal tangency replays
   26|       |/// `|d|^2 == (r_a - r_b)^2`. The row deliberately avoids square roots,
   27|       |/// normalization, and absolute values. Radius positivity, noncoincident
   28|       |/// centers, and containment policy are retained domain/preflight obligations
   29|       |/// rather than hidden tolerance checks, following the exact replay boundary.
   30|  3.79k|pub(crate) fn circle_circle_tangent_exprs(
   31|  3.79k|    first_center: &[Expr; 2],
   32|  3.79k|    first_radius: Expr,
   33|  3.79k|    second_center: &[Expr; 2],
   34|  3.79k|    second_radius: Expr,
   35|  3.79k|    external: bool,
   36|  3.79k|) -> CircleCircleTangentExprs {
   37|  3.79k|    let center_delta = [
   38|  3.79k|        second_center[0].clone() - first_center[0].clone(),
   39|  3.79k|        second_center[1].clone() - first_center[1].clone(),
   40|  3.79k|    ];
   41|  3.79k|    let branch_radius = if external {
   42|  2.25k|        first_radius + second_radius
   43|       |    } else {
   44|  1.54k|        first_radius - second_radius
   45|       |    };
   46|       |
   47|  3.79k|    CircleCircleTangentExprs {
   48|  3.79k|        tangency: squared_norm2(&center_delta) - branch_radius.clone() * branch_radius,
   49|  3.79k|    }
   50|  3.79k|}
   51|       |
   52|  3.79k|fn squared_norm2(v: &[Expr; 2]) -> Expr {
   53|  3.79k|    v[0].clone() * v[0].clone() + v[1].clone() * v[1].clone()
   54|  3.79k|}

    1|       |//! Exact cubic-Bezier point and tangent expressions for sketch constraints.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module keeps the differential part of retained cubic constraints out
    4|       |//! of the general sketch handle/diagnostic layer. The formulas are Bernstein
    5|       |//! polynomials: point evaluation uses the cubic basis, tangent evaluation uses
    6|       |//! the derivative control net `3(P1-P0), 3(P2-P1), 3(P3-P2)`, and second
    7|       |//! derivative evaluation uses the quadratic derivative control net
    8|       |//! `6(P2-2P1+P0), 6(P3-2P2+P1)`. Keeping these expressions symbolic follows
    9|       |//! the exact-geometric-computation model: curve construction and parameter choice remain retained
   10|       |//! objects, while exact replay certifies the incidence and tangent rows. The
   11|       |//! Bernstein/de Casteljau model follows the Bernstein/de Casteljau construction.
   12|       |
   13|       |use crate::symbolic::Expr;
   14|       |
   15|       |/// Exact point and differential expressions for a retained cubic Bezier curve.
   16|       |#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
   17|       |pub(crate) struct CubicPointTangentExprs {
   18|       |    /// Cubic Bezier point `B(t)`.
   19|       |    pub(crate) point: [Expr; 2],
   20|       |    /// Cubic Bezier derivative `B'(t)`.
   21|       |    pub(crate) tangent: [Expr; 2],
   22|       |    /// Cubic Bezier second derivative `B''(t)`.
   23|       |    pub(crate) second_derivative: [Expr; 2],
   24|       |}

   27|       |///

   29|       |/// function deliberately does not impose `0 <= t <= 1`; segment-domain policy
   30|       |/// belongs to explicit sketch parameter domains or range constraints.
   31|  30.1k|pub(crate) fn cubic_point_tangent_exprs(
   32|  30.1k|    p0: &[Expr; 2],
   33|  30.1k|    p1: &[Expr; 2],
   34|  30.1k|    p2: &[Expr; 2],
   35|  30.1k|    p3: &[Expr; 2],
   36|  30.1k|    parameter: Expr,
   37|  30.1k|) -> CubicPointTangentExprs {
   38|  30.1k|    let one_minus_t = Expr::int(1) - parameter.clone();
   39|  30.1k|    let b0 = one_minus_t.clone() * one_minus_t.clone() * one_minus_t.clone();
   40|  30.1k|    let b1 = Expr::int(3) * one_minus_t.clone() * one_minus_t.clone() * parameter.clone();
   41|  30.1k|    let b2 = Expr::int(3) * one_minus_t.clone() * parameter.clone() * parameter.clone();
   42|  30.1k|    let b3 = parameter.clone() * parameter.clone() * parameter.clone();
   43|  30.1k|    let q0 = [
   44|  30.1k|        Expr::int(3) * (p1[0].clone() - p0[0].clone()),
   45|  30.1k|        Expr::int(3) * (p1[1].clone() - p0[1].clone()),
   46|  30.1k|    ];
   47|  30.1k|    let q1 = [
   48|  30.1k|        Expr::int(3) * (p2[0].clone() - p1[0].clone()),
   49|  30.1k|        Expr::int(3) * (p2[1].clone() - p1[1].clone()),
   50|  30.1k|    ];
   51|  30.1k|    let q2 = [

    1|       |//! Sketch parameter-domain preflight certificates.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! This module checks retained sketch parameter domains before residual
    4|       |//! lowering or numerical iteration. The checks deliberately return report rows
    5|       |//! instead of mutating values or applying epsilon repairs: the exact Exact
    6|       |//! Geometric Computation model requires certified decisions or explicit
    7|       |//! uncertainty; see the exact-geometric-computation model. The separation between domain
    8|       |//! preconditions and residual certificates is also consistent with Moore's
    9|       |//! interval-analysis discipline for validated numerical computation.
   10|       |
   11|       |use std::cmp::Ordering;
   12|       |
   13|       |use hyperlimit::{PredicatePolicy, compare_reals};
   14|       |use hyperreal::Real;
   15|       |
   16|       |use crate::sketch::{SketchParameterDomain, SketchParameterHandle, SketchSolveProblem};
   17|       |
   18|       |/// Stable family name for a sketch parameter-domain check.
   19|       |#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
   20|       |pub enum SketchParameterDomainKind {
   21|       |    /// Exact lock value.
   22|       |    Locked,
   23|       |    /// Closed lower/upper bounds.
   24|       |    Bounded,
   25|       |    /// Nonnegative scalar.
   26|       |    Nonnegative,
   27|       |    /// Strictly positive scalar.
   28|       |    Positive,
   29|       |    /// Nonzero scalar.
   30|       |    Nonzero,
   31|       |    /// Closed angular range.
   32|       |    AngularRange,
   33|       |    /// Strictly positive period.
   34|       |    Periodic,
   35|       |}
   36|       |

    1|       |//! Sketch-level failed-constraint diagnostics.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Generic residual diagnostics know only lowered row indices. Retained sketch
    4|       |//! callers need the same exact evidence grouped back onto semantic source
    5|       |//! constraints and generated-row provenance. This module performs that join
    6|       |//! without introducing tolerances: it lowers the sketch, runs exact candidate
    7|       |//! diagnostics, then replays the residual-index mapping carried by
    8|       |//! [`crate::sketch::SketchGeneratedRow`]. The design follows the exact Exact
    9|       |//! Geometric Computation boundary: numerical state may be a proposal, but
   10|       |//! failed-constraint evidence is accepted only as exact/certified diagnostics
   11|       |//! or explicit lowering failure. The source-facing
   12|       |//! grouping mirrors the user-visible failed-constraint reporting described in
   13|       |//! the geometric-constraint-solver model.
   14|       |

  109|       |/// Diagnose failed constraints for a retained sketch with explicit settings.
  110|       |///
  111|       |/// The function lowers the sketch once, certifies the current exact parameter
  112|       |/// values as a candidate, and maps each failed lowered row back to the retained
  113|       |/// source constraint that generated it. Rows that did not lower are reported

  124|    778|    let exact = diagnose_failed_constraints_from_certification(
  125|    778|        &analysis,

  127|    778|        rank_min_precision,

    1|       |//! Exact oriented 2D angle-equality packages for sketch constraints.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! A retained oriented angle is represented by the two scalar invariants of a
    4|       |//! line pair, `(dot(a, b), cross(a, b))`. For nondegenerate line carriers this
    5|       |//! vector is a positive scale of `(cos(theta), sin(theta))`, so equality of two
    6|       |//! oriented angles can be certified without `atan2`, inverse trigonometry, or
    7|       |//! primitive-float normalization. That keeps the decision boundary at exact
    8|       |//! replay, as required by the exact-geometric-computation model. The explicit angle-vector and branch
    9|       |//! split follows the retained-constraint vocabulary used by geometric constraint solvers.
   10|       |
   11|       |use crate::symbolic::Expr;
   12|       |
   13|       |/// Exact residual expressions for a retained oriented 2D equal-angle relation.
   14|       |#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
   15|       |pub(crate) struct OrientedAngleExprs {
   16|       |    /// Equation certifying that the two angle vectors are collinear:
   17|       |    /// `dot(a,b) * cross(c,d) - cross(a,b) * dot(c,d) == 0`.
   18|       |    pub(crate) angle_vector_collinear: Expr,
   19|       |    /// Inequality certifying that the collinear angle vectors point along the
   20|       |    /// same oriented branch rather than the supplemental branch.
   21|       |    pub(crate) same_branch: Expr,
   22|       |}
   23|       |
   24|       |/// Build exact rows for equality of two oriented 2D angles.
   25|       |///
   26|       |/// The inputs are the four unnormalized line directions for the angles
   27|       |/// `(a,b)` and `(c,d)`. The proof package is:
   28|       |///
   29|       |/// - angle-vector collinearity, `(dot_ab, cross_ab) x (dot_cd, cross_cd) == 0`;
   30|       |/// - same-branch predicate, `(dot_ab, cross_ab) . (dot_cd, cross_cd) >= 0`.
   31|       |///
   32|       |/// No row divides by a line length. Zero-length line carriers therefore remain
   33|       |/// explicit entity-domain obligations instead of disappearing behind a
   34|       |/// normalized angle.
   35|  3.17k|pub(crate) fn oriented_angle_exprs(
   36|  3.17k|    a: &[Expr; 2],
   37|  3.17k|    b: &[Expr; 2],
   38|  3.17k|    c: &[Expr; 2],
   39|  3.17k|    d: &[Expr; 2],
   40|  3.17k|) -> OrientedAngleExprs {
   41|  3.17k|    let first_dot = dot2(a, b);
   42|  3.17k|    let first_cross = cross2(a, b);
   43|  3.17k|    let second_dot = dot2(c, d);
   44|  3.17k|    let second_cross = cross2(c, d);
   45|       |
   46|  3.17k|    OrientedAngleExprs {
   47|  3.17k|        angle_vector_collinear: first_dot.clone() * second_cross.clone()
   48|  3.17k|            - first_cross.clone() * second_dot.clone(),
   49|  3.17k|        same_branch: first_dot * second_dot + first_cross * second_cross,
   50|  3.17k|    }
   51|  3.17k|}
   52|       |
   53|  6.35k|fn dot2(a: &[Expr; 2], b: &[Expr; 2]) -> Expr {
   54|  6.35k|    a[0].clone() * b[0].clone() + a[1].clone() * b[1].clone()
   55|  6.35k|}
   56|       |

    2|       |//!

    8|       |//! source object, while candidate acceptance is decided by exact polynomial
    9|       |//! replay. The normal axis is derived from the standard unit-quaternion frame
   10|       |//! matrix described by the standard unit-quaternion construction.

   18|       |    /// Unit-quaternion guard for the retained workplane normal.
   19|       |    pub(crate) unit_guard: Expr,
   20|       |    /// Equation certifying that the midpoint lies on the workplane.
   21|       |    pub(crate) midpoint_plane: Expr,

   28|       |///
   29|       |/// For points `a` and `b`, workplane origin `o`, and unit normal `n`, symmetry
   30|       |/// is certified by `(a + b - 2o) . n == 0` and `(a - b) x n == 0`. The first
   31|       |/// row puts the midpoint on the plane without constructing a rounded midpoint;
   32|       |/// the second package proves the connecting segment is normal to the plane
   33|       |/// without dividing by `|a-b|` or normalizing the quaternion with floats.
   34|  1.59k|pub(crate) fn workplane_point_symmetry_exprs(
   35|  1.59k|    origin: &[Expr; 3],
   36|  1.59k|    quaternion: &[Expr; 4],

   38|  1.59k|    b: &[Expr; 3],
   39|  1.59k|) -> WorkplaneSymmetryExprs {
   40|  1.59k|    let (_, _, normal_axis) = quaternion_frame_axes_expr(quaternion);
   41|  1.59k|    let doubled_midpoint_delta = [
   42|  1.59k|        a[0].clone() + b[0].clone() - Expr::int(2) * origin[0].clone(),
   43|  1.59k|        a[1].clone() + b[1].clone() - Expr::int(2) * origin[1].clone(),
   44|  1.59k|        a[2].clone() + b[2].clone() - Expr::int(2) * origin[2].clone(),
   45|  1.59k|    ];
   46|  1.59k|    let point_offset = [
   47|  1.59k|        a[0].clone() - b[0].clone(),
   48|  1.59k|        a[1].clone() - b[1].clone(),
   49|  1.59k|        a[2].clone() - b[2].clone(),

    1|       |//! Exact workplane frame facts and point lift/project helpers.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! SolveSpace-style workplanes are retained objects: an origin point plus a
    4|       |//! quaternion-like normal carrier. This module keeps that object structure
    5|       |//! visible and emits report-bearing frame facts instead of silently normalizing
    6|       |//! with primitive floats. That follows the exact-geometric-computation
    7|       |//! boundary: geometric decisions consume certified facts or return explicit
    8|       |//! uncertainty.
    9|       |//!
   10|       |//! The `U/V/N` frame below uses the standard unit-quaternion rotation matrix;
   11|       |//! the exact polynomial form is evaluated only after the retained quaternion's
   12|       |//! squared norm is certified to be one. See the unit-quaternion construction.
   13|       |
   14|       |use std::cmp::Ordering;
   15|       |
   16|       |use hyperlimit::{PredicatePolicy, compare_reals};
   17|       |use hyperreal::Real;

   44|       |        /// Expected retained family.

   46|       |    },

   58|       |}

  438|       |

  440|    815|    let xx = x.clone() * x.clone();
  441|    815|    let yy = y.clone() * y.clone();
  442|    815|    let zz = z.clone() * z.clone();
  443|    815|    let wx = w.clone() * x.clone();
  444|    815|    let wy = w.clone() * y.clone();
  445|    815|    let wz = w.clone() * z.clone();
  446|    815|    let xy = x.clone() * y.clone();
  447|    815|    let xz = x.clone() * z.clone();
  448|    815|    let yz = y.clone() * z.clone();

    1|       |//! Nonlinear solver-block analysis.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! `ProblemAnalysis` records row facts close to the model. `SolverBlock`
    4|       |//! is the next scheduling layer: it partitions active rows into the categories
    5|       |//! a nonlinear backend needs before it decides whether to run substitution,
    6|       |//! affine elimination, polynomial handling, or an external numeric proposal
    7|       |//! engine. This follows the exact guidance that exact geometry needs packages above
    8|       |//! BigNumber for expressions and geometric objects, and mirrors SolveSpace's
    9|       |//! explicit substitution/soluble-equation/Jacobian passes while keeping
   10|       |//! primitive numeric iteration outside the proof boundary.
   11|       |
   12|       |use crate::analysis::{ConstraintFacts, ProblemAnalysis};
   13|       |use crate::symbolic::ExprDegree;
   14|       |
   15|       |/// Solver scheduling class for one source constraint row.
   16|       |#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
   17|       |pub enum SolverBlockRowKind {
   18|       |    /// Source row is disabled and not part of the active solve.
   19|       |    Inactive,
   20|       |    /// Active constant row proved exactly zero before iteration.
   21|       |    ConstantCertifiedZero,
   22|       |    /// Active constant row proved nonzero before iteration.
   23|       |    ConstantCertifiedContradiction,
   24|       |    /// Active constant row whose sign cannot be certified structurally.
   25|       |    ConstantUnknown,

    1|       |//! Exact constrained-axis resultants for dense polynomial tensors.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! The curve-specific resultant helpers cover two, three, and four variables
    4|       |//! with convenient typed tensors.  Exact recursive constructions eventually
    5|       |//! need one more selected source field, however, and duplicating another fixed
    6|       |//! rank only postpones the same boundary.  This module supplies the rank-
    7|       |//! independent primitive: eliminate any tensor axis against one exact
    8|       |//! univariate constraint, retaining every other axis and every shared-root
    9|       |//! correlation.
   10|       |//!
   11|       |//! Resultants are evaluated on an exact integer tensor grid and reconstructed

    1|       |//! Shared work accounting for one synchronous exact computation.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! A budget limits admitted root-subdivision and algebraic-promotion attempts.
    4|       |//! It does not select a predicate policy or permit approximation. Exhaustion
    5|       |//! is a resource failure, not a proof that a value is zero or unsupported.
    6|       |//!
    7|       |//! These units count algorithmic work, not elapsed time, bytes, or scalar
    8|       |//! arithmetic. A single admitted attempt can still manipulate large exact
    9|       |//! coefficients. Only instrumented paths participate; this is not yet a
   10|       |//! whole-solver resource bound. Callers must not infer a hard time limit from
   11|       |//! the counters. Work outside a budget keeps its existing behavior.
   12|       |//!
   13|       |//! Current instrumentation includes native univariate Sturm isolation and
   14|       |//! singleton refinement, represented-root sign-change refinement, tensor-image
   15|       |//! promotion, and Hypercurve's Bernstein/Sturm parameter subdivisions, native
   16|       |//! recursive-field refinements, and selected-fiber/local-field promotions.
   17|       |//! The shared ordered-field Bernstein isolator, selected-fiber Sturm isolator,
   18|       |//! reusable fiber-root refiner, and retained local-field root refinements also
   19|       |//! participate. Polynomial, rational, and binary represented-root images charge
   20|       |//! their eliminant constructions; rational maps can reuse a cached eliminant
   21|       |//! without a new promotion charge. Constant and affine shortcuts need no
   22|       |//! promotion units. Selected-fiber polynomial-image norms, bivariate quotient
   23|       |//! norms, tagged tensor-fiber projections, bivariate system resultants,
   24|       |//! constrained tensor-axis resultants, fixed-rank three/four-variable norms,
   25|       |//! their subresultants, bivariate cofactor parameter lifts, common-component
   26|       |//! discovery, and axis-factor extraction also participate.
   27|       |//! Bivariate finite-fiber topology charges its construction entry, its existing
   28|       |//! projection/fiber operations, and connection-strip or outer-separator
   29|       |//! refinement attempts. Reusing a topology for a rational slice charges only
   30|       |//! the root work actually required; its earlier graph proof is not rebuilt.
   31|       |//! Other elimination entry points,
   32|       |//! remaining curve dispatch paths,
   33|       |//! scalar precision refinement, and arbitrary caller arithmetic are not
   34|       |//! comprehensively instrumented. Those paths need additional work
   35|       |//! before any whole-operation completion or time bound can be claimed.
   36|       |//!
   37|       |//! One promotion unit admits one instrumented projection entry, regardless of
   38|       |//! its degree or number of eliminated axes; root subdivisions performed inside
   39|       |//! it consume separate refinement units. Nested projection entries share the
   40|       |//! budget and charge additional units: a tagged tensor-fiber projection charges
   41|       |//! its entry, each needed tensor-axis resultant, and its final bivariate quotient
   42|       |//! norm. Degree-limit admission alone does not charge a bivariate or fixed-rank
   43|       |//! resultant. Fixed-rank subresultants also charge once before interpolation;
   44|       |//! a terminal-order subresultant reuses an input without a promotion charge.
   45|       |//! Cofactor parameter lifts charge one attempt after degree admission; their
   46|       |//! curve replay cache can reuse a completed report without a new charge and
   47|       |//! never retains a report of resource exhaustion.
   48|       |//! Common-component discovery charges once after degree admission, including
   49|       |//! its sampled-GCD and subresultant continuations. Axis-factor extraction
   50|       |//! charges once for a nonzero system and again before a projective-scale retry.
   51|       |//! Successive factor removals share the allowance. Saturation, multiplicity
   52|       |//! reduction, selector splitting, and trivariate factor normalization preserve
   53|       |//! exhaustion instead of publishing partially processed supports or factors.
   54|       |//! Usage depends on retained evidence,
   55|       |//! representation, and algorithm version. A ready proof may require no units.
   56|       |//! Resource blockers must not be retained as mathematical capability facts.
   57|       |//! Budgeted rational-map requests may read existing elimination caches but
   58|       |//! leave new eliminants uncached, including failed construction attempts.
   59|       |//!
   60|       |//! Nested scopes share their actual charges: an inner budget cannot replenish
   61|       |//! its parent. A failed charge spends no units. An exhausted scope cannot
   62|       |//! publish a successful result, even if an intermediate caller ignores the
   63|       |//! failure. A smaller inner budget may fail without exhausting its parent.
   64|       |//!
   65|       |//! Scopes are thread-local and restore on return and unwinding. They do not
   66|       |//! follow a future or propagate to spawned threads; configure each synchronous
